a1.say: Let's solve Product of Everything Else, using the Left and Right Running Products approach.

a1.cap: Return an array res where res[i] is the product of every element of nums except nums[i]. Do it in O(n) time without division.
a1.say: Return an array res where res at i is the product of every element of nums except nums at i. Do it in O of n time without division.

lines: Return an array res where res[i] is the product of every element of nums except nums[i]. Do it in O(n) time without division.

a1.cap: For example, with nums = [1,2,3,4], the answer is [24,12,8,6].
a1.say: For example, with nums equals 1, 2, 3, 4, the answer is 24, 12, 8, 6.

a1.cap: The answer at i is the product of everything to its left times everything to its right.
First sweep left to right, writing the running product of the left side into the result. Then sweep right to left with a second running product for the right side, multiplying it in.
Let's walk through it with nums = [1,2,3,4].
a1.say: Let's walk through it with nums equals 1, 2, 3, 4.

a1.cap: Everything left of index 0 multiplies to 1.
Everything left of index 1 multiplies to 1.
Everything left of index 2 multiplies to 2.
Everything left of index 3 multiplies to 6.
Times everything right of index 3 (1) gives 6.
Times everything right of index 2 (4) gives 8.
Times everything right of index 1 (12) gives 12.
Times everything right of index 0 (24) gives 24.
Time complexity is O(n) and extra space is O(1) extra. Two passes; apart from the output array we only keep one running number.
a1.say: Time complexity is O of n and extra space is O of one extra. Two passes; apart from the output array we only keep one running number.

a1.cap: That's the Left & Right Running Products approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
